proof:
Notation: fix n, l, P. Write G := G(P) and v_a := P e_a. For xi, eta in R^n (functions Fin n -> R), xi . eta = sum_a xi_a eta_a and (M xi)_a = sum_b M_{ab} xi_b.

1. Quadratic form of G. For every xi, xi . (G xi) = sum_a sum_b xi_a <v_a, v_b> xi_b = <sum_a xi_a v_a, sum_b xi_b v_b> = ||P(sum_a xi_a e_a)||^2. This uses bilinearity and symmetry of the real inner product and linearity of P (P(sum_a xi_a e_a) = sum_a xi_a v_a). In particular xi . (G xi) >= 0.

2. Trivial kernel of I + sG for s >= 0. Let s >= 0 and suppose (I + sG) xi = 0. Taking the dot product with xi gives 0 = xi . xi + s xi . (G xi) = sum_a xi_a^2 + s ||P(sum_a xi_a e_a)||^2. Both summands are >= 0 (s >= 0 and step 1), so sum_a xi_a^2 = 0. A sum of squares vanishes only if every term does, so xi = 0.

3. Nonvanishing determinant. For a square matrix M over R, det M = 0 iff M xi = 0 for some xi != 0 (Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff). By step 2, det(I + sG) != 0 for every s >= 0.

4. Continuity. h(s) := det(I + sG) is continuous in s in R: s -> I + sG is continuous entrywise and det is a polynomial in the entries (Continuous.matrix_det). Also h(0) = det I = 1.

5. Intermediate value theorem. Suppose det(I + G) = h(1) <= 0. Then h(1) <= 0 <= 1 = h(0) and h is continuous on [0, 1]. The intermediate value theorem (intermediate_value_Icc') gives s in [0, 1] with h(s) = 0. Since s >= 0, this contradicts step 3. Hence det(I + G) = h(1) > 0. QED

Source: parent step 1. The input is the same inequality xi^T (I + G) xi >= |xi|^2. The conclusion is reached by the continuity argument because Matrix.PosDef, Matrix.PosSemidef, Matrix.PosDef.det_pos, Matrix.gram and Matrix.posSemidef_gram are NOT imported by GMT.Ch05.Submission (checked at the pin: unknown constants), and the Submission imports must stay unchanged.
